mainTopic: When the כהן משיח brings his own פר: it requires a mistaken ruling like the ציבור, and he is atoned for with the ציבור when he errs together with them.
overview: The amud asks when the כהן משיח (the anointed כהן גדול) brings his פר. Does he need a mistaken ruling (העלם דבר) together with an unwitting act, like the ציבור? Or is an unwitting act alone enough, like the נשיא? Comparisons pull both ways. The ציבור and the משיח both bring a פר and no אשם תלוי. The נשיא and the משיח both bring a שעירה for עבודה זרה and an אשם ודאי. The פסוק 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם' settles it: the משיח is like the ציבור. Another phrase, 'עַל חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא', limits him to his own sin, not to sins others commit because of his ruling. The גמרא then explains why he brings no אשם תלוי, and why the ברייתא mentioned that rule only in passing. A new משנה teaches that a משיח who errs alone brings his own קרבן, while one who errs with the ציבור is atoned for with them. The גמרא proves this from a ברייתא and then begins asking what exact case counts as the משיח ruling on his own. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Comparing the anointed כהן to the public
steps.stepSummary: The ציבור and the משיח both stand apart from a regular יחיד. So, like the ציבור, the משיח should be liable only for העלם דבר together with שגגת מעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The public is different from a regular person, and the anointed כהן is also different from a regular person. The public only brings a קרבן when a mistaken ruling leads to an unwitting act. So the anointed כהן should also bring only in that case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proposes a comparison. Since both the ציבור and the משיח are 'taken out' of the normal rules for an individual, the משיח should follow the ציבור's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular יחיד brings a female sheep or goat for a sin, but the ציבור and the משיח both bring something different. That shared difference is used as a bridge. Whatever is true of the ציבור, that it needs a mistaken ruling plus an action, should also be true of the משיח.

keyTerms.meaning: The community as a whole
The anointed כהן גדול
Taken out of the category of a regular individual
A law was 'hidden', meaning a mistaken ruling was given
Doing a forbidden act by mistake

phrases.english: The public is taken out of the category of an individual,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the attempt to derive the rule for the משיח through comparison.
steps.raayaObject: That a משיח is liable only for העלם דבר עם שגגת מעשה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to the ציבור, since both differ from a regular יחיד

steps.title: A competing comparison to the king
steps.stepSummary: The נשיא is also 'taken out' of the category of a יחיד. He brings a קרבן for a plain שגגת מעשה, so maybe the משיח should too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe go a different way. The king is also different from a regular person, and so is the anointed כהן. The king brings a קרבן for an unwitting act even without a mistaken ruling. So the anointed כהן should also bring for an unwitting act without a mistaken ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on the first comparison. It shows that the same reasoning could just as easily link the משיח to the נשיא, which gives the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first comparison only worked because the ציבור and the משיח both differ from a יחיד. But the נשיא also differs from a יחיד, and he needs no mistaken ruling. Because the same reasoning gives two opposite results, the first comparison alone proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or go this way': a formula that offers a competing comparison
The king or leader
Without

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a final ruling that the משיח is like the נשיא. The ברייתא is only showing that both comparisons seem equally strong, so it needs a better way to decide.

phrases.english: Or go this way:

without a hidden matter,
so too, an anointed priest brings for an unwitting action
without a hidden matter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Weakens Step 1 by offering an equally valid comparison with the opposite result.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the משיח to the ציבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being 'taken out' of the category of a יחיד also applies to the נשיא, who needs no העלם דבר. So this shared trait cannot decide the question.

steps.title: Looking for the closer match: the bull and no אשם תלוי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא looks for whom the משיח really resembles. Like the ציבור, he brings a פר and never brings an אשם תלוי, so he should need העלם דבר עם שגגת מעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let's see whom he is more like. The public brings a bull and does not bring a doubtful guilt offering. The anointed כהן also brings a bull and does not bring a doubtful guilt offering. So, just like the public, he should only be liable when a mistaken ruling leads to an unwitting act.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the simple comparisons cancel each other out, the גמרא now looks for stronger points of similarity. It finds two that connect the משיח to the ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a sharper test than before. The משיח and the ציבור share two specific features: they bring the same animal (a פר), and neither ever brings an אשם תלוי. Because of these closer ties, the ציבור's rule should apply to the משיח.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let us see whom it resembles': looking for the closer comparison
A bull
A provisional guilt offering, brought when unsure whether one sinned

and an anointed priest atones with a bull,

phrases.english: except for a hidden matter together with an unwitting action,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר עִם שִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה.

steps.title: The king matches too: the female goat and the definite guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: The נשיא and the משיח both bring a שעירה for עבודה זרה and both bring an אשם ודאי. So maybe the משיח is like the נשיא and brings for a plain שגגת מעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe go a different way. The king brings a female goat for idol worship and brings a definite guilt offering. The anointed כהן also brings a female goat for idol worship and brings a definite guilt offering. So, just as the king brings for an unwitting act alone, the anointed כהן should also bring for an unwitting act alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the closer comparison of Step 3. It finds two equally specific features that connect the משיח to the נשיא instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For עבודה זרה, the ציבור brings a פר and never brings an אשם ודאי. The נשיא and the משיח, however, both bring a שעירה and both bring an אשם ודאי. These two shared points are just as strong as the ones in Step 3, so the question is open again.

keyTerms.meaning: A female goat
Idol worship
A definite guilt offering, for sins like misusing הקדש or robbery

steps.whatToRemember: Each side now has two specific points in its favor. The ציבור and the משיח share a פר and no אשם תלוי. The נשיא and the משיח share a שעירה for עבודה זרה and an אשם ודאי. So the comparisons alone have not settled the question.

phrases.english: Or go this way:
The king brings a female goat for idol worship
and brings a definite guilt offering,
and an anointed priest brings a female goat for idol worship
and brings a definite guilt offering.
Just as a king brings an offering for an unwitting action,
so too, an anointed priest brings an offering for an unwitting action.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ כְּלָךְ לְדֶרֶךְ זוֹ: נָשִׂיא מֵבִיא שְׂעִירָה בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters Step 3 with equally specific similarities between the משיח and the נשיא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The closer comparison of the משיח to the ציבור in Step 3
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משיח shares with the נשיא a שעירה for עבודה זרה and an אשם ודאי, which the ציבור lacks. So the comparison to the נשיא is just as strong, and it points to liability for שגגת מעשה alone.

steps.title: A פסוק settles it: the משיח is like the ציבור
steps.stepSummary: Since logic could support either side, the פסוק 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם' decides that the משיח is compared to the ציבור. So he brings a קרבן only for הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר עִם שִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'so as to bring guilt upon the people.' This shows the anointed priest is like the community. Just as the community brings a קרבן only when a mistaken ruling leads to an unknowing act, so too the anointed priest brings a קרבן only for a mistaken ruling together with an unknowing act.
steps.whatsHappening: The two logical comparisons were evenly matched, so the ברייתא brings a פסוק to decide the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 3 and 4 showed that the משיח looks like the ציבור in some ways and like the נשיא in others. Logic alone cannot break the tie. The words 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם' (the guilt of the people) link the משיח to the ציבור, so he follows the ציבור's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; introduces a proof from a פסוק
'So as to bring guilt upon the people' (ויקרא 4:3)
A 'hidden matter': a mistaken ruling about the law
Doing a forbidden act without knowing it is forbidden
The anointed כהן גדול
The community as a whole

steps.whatToRemember: The משיח is like the ציבור: he brings his פר only when his own mistaken ruling led to his own unknowing act.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the rule in the משנה that the משיח's קרבן depends on a mistaken ruling, unlike a regular יחיד or the נשיא.

phrases.english: The verse states: "so as to bring guilt upon the people"
This shows the anointed priest is like the community.
Just as the community does not bring a קרבן
except for a mistaken ruling
together with an unknowing act,
so too the anointed priest does not bring one
except for a mistaken ruling
together with an unknowing act.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם״, הֲרֵי הוּא מָשִׁיחַ כְּצִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks the tie between the comparison to the ציבור (Step 3) and the comparison to the נשיא (Step 4) by bringing a פסוק.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משיח is like the ציבור and brings only for a mistaken ruling together with an unknowing act.

steps.title: Should the משיח be liable when others follow his ruling?
steps.stepSummary: If the משיח is like the ציבור, then maybe he should also be liable when other people act on his mistaken ruling, the way the court is liable when the people follow its ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe say this: just as with the community, if the court ruled and people acted on its ruling, they are liable, so too with the anointed priest, if he ruled and others acted on his ruling, he should be liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the new comparison further and asks whether it should carry over another rule of the ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the ציבור, the court makes the ruling but the people do the act, and a קרבן is still brought. If the משיח is fully like the ציבור, then his ruling should make him liable even when only others act on it. The challenge tests how far the comparison reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead; introduces a possible other reading
He ruled; gave a legal decision
A legal ruling
They are liable (to bring a קרבן)

phrases.english: Say instead: just as with the community, if the court ruled
and people acted following its ruling, they are liable,
so too the anointed priest, when he ruled
and others acted following his ruling, he should be liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: מָה צִבּוּר הוֹרָה וְעָשׂוּ אַחֲרָיו בְּהוֹרָאָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the comparison from Step 5 should go.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the משיח to the ציבור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משיח is fully like the ציבור, he should be liable even when others act on his ruling, just as the ציבור's קרבן comes when people act on the court's ruling.

steps.title: He brings only for his own sin
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'וְהִקְרִיב עַל חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא' limits the משיח to his own sin. He brings nothing when others sin because of his ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'Then he shall offer for his sin that he sinned.' He brings a קרבן for what he himself sinned, and does not bring one for what others sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with another phrase from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'his sin that he sinned' show that the משיח's קרבן is only for an act he did himself. So the comparison to the ציבור applies to needing a mistaken ruling, but not to being liable for other people's acts.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall offer for his sin' (ויקרא 4:3)
He sinned
Others; other people

steps.whatToRemember: The משיח's ruling must lead to his own act. If only others act on his ruling, he brings nothing.

phrases.english: The verse states:

For what he himself sinned he brings a קרבן,

steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting phrase in the פסוק narrows the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משיח is like the ציבור in every way, so he would be liable when others act on his ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is like the ציבור only in needing a mistaken ruling. He brings only for a sin he did himself.

steps.title: Where do we learn the משיח brings no אשם תלוי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the earlier statement that the משיח brings a פר and no אשם תלוי, and asks for the source of the second half.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: An anointed priest atones with a bull and does not bring an אשם תלוי. From where does he know that he does not bring an אשם תלוי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a statement used earlier in Step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 used the fact that the משיח never brings an אשם תלוי to compare him to the ציבור. Now the גמרא wants to know where that fact itself comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: A bull; the משיח's sin-offering
A 'hanging' guilt-offering, brought when one is unsure if he sinned
From where does he know this?

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This points back to the statement the ברייתא made in Step 3.

phrases.english: An anointed priest atones with a bull

From where does he know

steps.title: An אשם תלוי is only for one whose mistake and sin are the same
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק of אשם תלוי, 'עַל שִׁגְגָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר שָׁגָג', applies only to someone whose mistake is the sin itself. The משיח's mistake is in his ruling, which is separate from his act, so he is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the priest shall atone for him for his error that he erred.' This means someone whose sin and error are the same. That excludes the anointed priest, whose error and sin are not the same, as it is written 'so as to bring guilt upon the people,' meaning the anointed priest is like the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with the פסוק about אשם תלוי and explains why the משיח does not fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a regular person, the mistake and the sin are one thing: he did the act without knowing. For the משיח, the mistake is his wrong ruling, and the sin is the act he did because of it. Since the פסוק 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם' makes him like the ציבור (needing a ruling), his mistake and sin are always two things, so the אשם תלוי does not apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: An honest mistake
Here: the sin itself
Equal; the same
Excluded; left out
As it is written

steps.whatToRemember: The משיח never brings an אשם תלוי because his mistake (the ruling) and his sin (the act) are two separate things.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם' from Step 5 appears again here. It is not a new proof of the same point. It is used to explain why the משיח's mistake and sin are not the same.

steps.title: But the ברייתא had not yet quoted 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 9. The 'no אשם תלוי' rule depends on 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם', but the ברייתא used that rule as a point of comparison (step 3) before it ever quoted that פסוק (step 5).
steps.simpleTranslation: 'So as to bring guilt upon the people'? Up to this point he hasn't even said that פסוק!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the answer it just gave. If 'no אשם תלוי' comes from 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם', how could the ברייתא use it in step 3 to compare the משיח to the ציבור, when it had not yet quoted that פסוק?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 showed that the משיח is exempt from אשם תלוי only because 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם' makes his mistake lie in his ruling. But at step 3 the ברייתא had not yet brought that פסוק, and it was still trying to prove by logic that he needs a ruling. So it could not yet use 'no אשם תלוי' as a reason to compare him to the ציבור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So as to bring guilt upon the people.' The פסוק that compares the משיח to the ציבור
Up to this point
He has not said it

phrases.english: 'So as to bring guilt upon the people'?

phrases.notes: The ברייתא used the אשם rule in its comparison before it ever quoted this פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 9's derivation by noting that the ברייתא used the 'no אשם תלוי' rule in step 3 before citing 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'no אשם תלוי' (step 3) as a point of comparison, given that step 9 derives that rule from 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exemption from אשם תלוי depends on 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם', which the ברייתא had not yet quoted. So it is circular to use that exemption to prove the משיח is like the ציבור.

steps.title: The mention of אשם was just said in passing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא could not really rely on 'no אשם תלוי' at that point, so the גמרא concludes that it mentioned the אשם only in passing. The real point of comparison was the פר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא mentioned the אשם only in passing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the extra phrase 'and no אשם תלוי'. The ברייתא simply mentioned it in passing; it was not the main point it was proving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that the משיח brings no אשם תלוי is still true, and it is learned as step 9 explained. But it was not really part of the ברייתא's comparison in step 3. The comparison rests on the פר, and the אשם was mentioned only in passing.

keyTerms.meaning: He took it up for nothing, meaning it was mentioned in passing
A guilt-offering brought when a person is unsure whether he sinned

steps.whatToRemember: The משיח brings a פר and no אשם תלוי. 'No אשם תלוי' is learned from 'עַל שִׁגְגָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר שָׁגָג' together with 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם', so in the ברייתא's comparison it is mentioned only in passing.

phrases.english: Rather, the אשם
he just mentioned in passing.
phrases.notes: Literally 'for nothing he took it up.' The rule is true; it just wasn't the point being proven here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10: the ברייתא mentioned אשם only in passing, so the comparison does not rely on it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The phrase is explained as an incidental mention, not a derived teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'no אשם תלוי' rule seemed to be one of the ברייתא's reasons for comparing the משיח to the ציבור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אשם תלוי was mentioned only in passing and is not a premise of the comparison. The comparison rests on the פר.

steps.title: משנה: the משיח alone versus the משיח together with the ציבור
steps.stepSummary: If the משיח rules and acts on his own, he brings his own קרבן. If he rules and acts together with the ציבור, he is atoned for along with them. The court and the משיח are liable only when they rule to cancel part of a מצוה, and this includes עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ruled by himself and acted by himself, he gets atonement by himself. If he ruled together with the ציבור and acted together with the ציבור, he gets atonement together with the ציבור. This is because a בית דין is not liable unless it rules to cancel part of a מצוה and keep part of it. The same is true for the משיח. And they are also not liable for עבודה זרה unless they rule to cancel part and keep part.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that when the משיח errs alone, he brings his own פר, but when he errs together with the בית דין and the people, the group's קרבן covers him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being part of the ציבור changes how the משיח gets his כפרה: he does not bring a separate פר. The משנה then adds a condition that applies to both the court and the משיח. They are liable only if the mistaken ruling cancels part of a מצוה, not the entire מצוה. This condition holds even for עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: He ruled, meaning he issued a הלכה decision
By himself, alone
He gets atonement
To cancel part of a מצוה and keep part of it
Idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'עִם הַצִּבּוּר' does not mean the משיח is off the hook. He still gets כפרה, but through the group's קרבן instead of his own פר.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
If he ruled by himself
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן משיח, the anointed כהן גדול.

phrases.english: and acted by himself,
he gets atonement by himself.
If he ruled with the public
phrases.notes: Here 'the public' means he ruled together with the בית דין.

phrases.english: and acted with the public,
he gets atonement with the public,
for the court is not liable
unless they rule to cancel part
and keep part,
and the same for the anointed priest,
and not for idol worship
unless they rule to cancel part
and keep part.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הוֹרָה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְעָשָׂה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A משיח who errs alone brings his own קרבן. A משיח who errs together with the ציבור is atoned for with them. Liability for both the court and the משיח requires a ruling that cancels only part of a מצוה, and this includes עבודה זרה.

steps.title: What is the source for this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the משנה's rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that the משיח is atoned for together with the ציבור when he errs along with them. It is setting up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know what shows that the משיח's כפרה depends on whether he acted alone or together with the ציבור. The answer comes from a ברייתא, which will start with a 'might I think' suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words? A request for the source

phrases.english: Gemara: From where are these matters known?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in the משנה of step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the משיח being atoned for together with the ציבור when he rules and acts with them.

steps.title: The ברייתא begins: maybe he brings his own פר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The ברייתא opens by suggesting that a משיח who erred with the ציבור might still bring his own פר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: If he ruled with the ציבור and acted with the ציבור, might I think he brings a פר for himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא as its source. The ברייתא first raises the possibility that the משיח brings his own פר even when he erred together with the ציבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יָכוֹל' signals a possibility that the ברייתא is about to test and will later reject. This is the opening of the answer, not its conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: Might I think? This introduces a possibility that will be rejected
A bull, the משיח's חטאת

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
If he ruled with the public
and acted with the public,
might I think he brings a bull for himself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 13's question by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא that will deal with whether the משיח brings his own פר when he erred with the ציבור. It opens with the possibility that he does.

steps.title: A comparison to the נשיא suggests the opposite outcome
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא makes a logical argument from the נשיא. The נשיא and the משיח each bring a different קרבן than an ordinary person. A נשיא who sins alone brings his own קרבן, and a נשיא who sins with the ציבור is atoned for with them. So the משיח should work the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is a logical argument. The נשיא is taken out of the category of an ordinary individual, and the משיח is taken out of the category of an ordinary individual. Just as the נשיא brings his own קרבן when he sins alone, and is atoned for with the ציבור when he sins with them, so too the משיח: when he sins alone he brings his own קרבן, and when he sins with the ציבור he is atoned for with them!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא presents a logical argument comparing the משיח to the נשיא. The ברייתא is still in the middle of its discussion, and this comparison will be tested next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the נשיא and the משיח have special קרבנות, unlike an ordinary person. A נשיא who sins together with the ציבור is covered by the ציבור's קרבן. The ברייתא argues that the משיח should therefore be covered the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is logical. This introduces a reasoning argument
The king or ruler, who brings a goat as his חטאת
Taken out of the category of an ordinary individual
Just as ... so too. The pattern of a comparison

steps.confusionAlert: This argument actually supports what the משנה says. But the ברייתא is not finished, so wait and see how it treats this reasoning before treating it as the final word.

phrases.english: And it is logical:
A king is taken out of the category of an individual
and an anointed priest is taken out of the category of an individual,
just as a king,
if he sinned by himself,
he brings by himself,
if he sinned with the public,
he gets atonement with the public.
So too an anointed priest,
if he sinned by himself,
he brings by himself,
if he sinned with the public,
he gets atonement with the public!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'יָכוֹל' of step 14 with a logical comparison to the נשיא, suggesting the משיח is atoned for with the ציבור.
steps.raayaObject: That a משיח who sins with the ציבור is atoned for together with them.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to the נשיא, who is also set apart from an ordinary individual and is atoned for with the ציבור when he sins with them.

steps.title: The proof from the נשיא is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes back on its own comparison. The נשיא gets atonement together with the ציבור on יום הכפורים, but the משיח does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. You can say this about the נשיא, because he is atoned for together with the ציבור on יום הכפורים. Can you say the same about the משיח, who is not atoned for together with the ציבור on יום הכפורים?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the logical argument from the last step. The נשיא and the משיח are not similar enough to compare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said: the נשיא can join the ציבור's atonement, so the משיח should be able to as well. The ברייתא answers that the נשיא already shares the ציבור's atonement on יום הכפורים, so it makes sense that he joins them here too. The משיח is separated from the ציבור on יום הכפורים, so maybe he is always separate.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you said…' The opening words of a rejection that points out how two cases are different.
The day of atonement
He gets atonement

phrases.english: No, if you said this about a king,
that makes sense, since he gets atonement with the public
on Yom Kippur.
Will you say the same about the anointed priest,
who does not get atonement with the public
on Yom Kippur?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison to the נשיא that was made in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The logical comparison between the נשיא and the משיח
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The נשיא shares the ציבור's atonement on יום הכפורים, and the משיח does not. So the two cases are not alike.

steps.title: Maybe the משיח always brings his own bull
steps.stepSummary: Because the משיח is separate on יום הכפורים, the ברייתא suggests he might bring his own פר even when he sins along with the ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he is not atoned for with the ציבור on יום הכפורים, you might think he brings a פר for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible conclusion that follows from the rejection. This sets up the פסוק that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the comparison to the נשיא fails, we lose our reason to include the משיח in the ציבור's atonement. So we might think he always brings his own פר, even when he sinned together with the ציבור.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
'You might think…' Introduces a possible idea that a פסוק will then reject.
A bull offering

phrases.english: Since he does not get atonement
with the public on Yom Kippur,
you might think he should bring a bull for himself?

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְאֵין מִתְכַּפֵּר לוֹ עִם הַצִּבּוּר בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, יָכוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the rejection in step 16 would seem to mean.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the משיח bring his own פר even when he sins together with the ציבור?

steps.title: The פסוק: 'for his sin that he sinned'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes a פסוק showing that the משיח's own פר is for a sin that is his alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'for his sin that he sinned.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a פסוק to settle the question from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'his sin that he sinned' point to a sin that belongs to him alone. So the separate פר of the משיח is only for a sin he did by himself.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches.' Introduces a פסוק that proves the point.
His sin

phrases.english: The verse states: "For his sin that he has sinned,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'you might think' of step 17 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The משיח's separate פר is limited to a sin he did alone.

steps.title: Alone, he brings his own; with the ציבור, he is atoned with them
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא sums up. If the משיח sins alone, he brings his own קרבן. If he sins with the ציבור, he is atoned for along with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he sinned by himself, he brings a קרבן by himself. If he sinned with the ציבור, he is atoned for with the ציבור.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out the final rule that comes from the פסוק. This is the source for the משנה's rule in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the question of step 13, 'where does the משנה's rule come from?' The proof from the נשיא failed, but the פסוק gives the same result directly.

keyTerms.meaning: 'How so?' Introduces the practical way the rule works.
By himself, alone

steps.whatToRemember: The משיח brings his own פר only for a sin he did alone. When he sins along with the ציבור, their קרבן covers him too. This comes from the פסוק 'עַל חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא', not from comparing him to the נשיא.

phrases.english: How so?

phrases.aramaic: חָטָא בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ – מֵבִיא בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: If he sinned by himself, he brings an offering by himself;

phrases.aramaic: חָטָא עִם הַצִּבּוּר – מִתְכַּפֵּר לוֹ עִם הַצִּבּוּר.
phrases.english: if he sinned with the public, he gets atonement with the public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the rule that comes out of the פסוק in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משיח brings his own פר only for a sin of his own. If he sinned with the ציבור, he is included in their atonement.

steps.title: What case is the משיח ruling on his own?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the real-life case. Its first suggestion is that the משיח is a top scholar and the court judges are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say the משיח is a distinguished scholar and the judges are not distinguished…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question and tries out a first possibility. This sets up the challenge that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a concrete picture of when the משיח counts as acting on his own and not with the court. It begins testing the options, starting with a gap in scholarly level between him and the judges.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the case?' Asks for the exact situation.
'If you say…' Introduces a suggestion that will be tested.
A distinguished scholar, qualified to rule on הלכה

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
phrases.notes: He is asking when the משיח counts as ruling and acting on his own, apart from the court.

phrases.english: If we say that he is a distinguished scholar
and they are not distinguished scholars,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the judges of the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the rule has a source, the גמרא asks what case it is talking about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact situation in which the משיח rules on his own, apart from the court.

steps.title: First option: then the rule is obvious
steps.stepSummary: If only the משיח is qualified, the court's ruling means nothing. So of course he brings his own קרבן, and everyone else brings a private one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then it is obvious that he is atoned for by himself, since their ruling is nothing. And each person would need to bring a כשבה or a שעירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first option. It says that in this case the rule would be too obvious to need teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling by judges who are not qualified does not count as a court ruling at all. So there is no shared ציבור offering, and each person who sinned brings the regular private חטאת. It would be obvious that the משיח brings his own.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is obvious.' Challenges a rule as too simple to need teaching.
Nothing at all, of no legal value
A female sheep or a female goat, the private חטאת of an ordinary person

phrases.english: it is obvious that he gets atonement by himself,
since their ruling is nothing at all.
And there is a need to bring a ewe or a female goat
for each and every one!
phrases.notes: Each person who acted on their ruling brings his own private חטאת, because there is no shared court offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the first case suggested in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the משיח is qualified and the judges are not
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In that case the court's ruling is worthless, so it is obvious that the משיח is separate. There is nothing to teach.

steps.title: Second option: then his ruling means nothing
steps.stepSummary: If the judges are qualified and the משיח is not, his ruling has no value. So why should he bring the special קרבן for acting on his own ruling?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they are distinguished and he is not, why is he atoned for by himself? His ruling is nothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the opposite case and challenges it too. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משיח's special פר is for acting on his own ruling. If he is not qualified to rule, his ruling does not count, and his sin is just a private mistake. So this case cannot explain the rule either.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
His own ruling

phrases.english: And if they are distinguished scholars
and he is not a distinguished scholar,
why does he get atonement by himself?

phrases.aramaic: הָא הוֹרָאָה דִּידֵיהּ וְלֹא כְּלוּם הִיא.
phrases.english: Isn't his ruling nothing at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי דְּאִינּוּן מוּפְלָאִין וְהוּא לָאו מוּפְלָא, אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the opposite case after the first one failed in step 21, and challenges it as well.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the judges are qualified and the משיח is not
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unqualified משיח's ruling has no legal value, so he should not bring the special קרבן for acting on his own ruling.
